sections.theory:
Example 3.12

The chances of a bomber hitting the target and missing the target are 3:2. Calculate the probability that the target will be hit at least once in five sorties.

Solution:

Given that p=\frac{3}{5}, q=\frac{2}{5}, n=5

X: denotes the number of hits.

$X=0,1,2,3,4,5$

So

$p(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix}{}^{5}_{x}C\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^x\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{5-x}, & x=0,1,2,3,4,5\\ 0, & \textit{otherwise}\end{matrix}\right.$

Now, P[at least one will hit the target] =1-P[no one will hit the target]

P(X\ge 1)=1-P[X=0]

=1-{}^{5}_{0}C\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^0\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{5-0}

=1-\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^5=1-0.01024=0.98976

لہٰذا

اب، P[کم از کم ایک ہدف پر لگے] =1-P[کوئی ہدف پر نہ لگے]

sections.title: 3.3.3 Properties of the binomial distribution — mean
sections.headingUrdu: 3.3.3 دو رقمی تقسیم کی خصوصیات — اوسط
sections.theory:
3.3.3 Properties of Binomial distribution

(i) Mean of Binomial distribution

By definition

\text{Mean}=E(X)=\sum_x x\,p(x)

=\sum_{x=0}^{n}x\,{}^{n}_{x}C\,p^xq^{n-x}

=0\,{}^{n}_{0}C\,p^0q^{n-0}+1\,{}^{n}_{1}C\,p^1q^{n-1}+2\,{}^{n}_{2}C\,p^2q^{n-2}+\ldots+n\,{}^{n}_{n}C\,p^nq^{n-n}

=0+npq^{n-1}+\ldots+np^n

=np\,[q^{n-1}+\ldots+p^{n-1}]

=np\,[q+p]^{n-1}

=np\,(1)^{n-1}\qquad\because p+q=1

=np

(ii) Variance of Binomial distribution

By definition

\text{Variance}=V(X)=E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2\qquad(A)

\text{As } E(X)=np\qquad(1)

\text{Now } E(X^2)=\Sigma x^2p(x)

=\sum_x[x(x-1)+x]\,p(x)\qquad\because x^2=x(x-1)+x
